STEP 1 - Scene: Sliced cooked sausage (looks like a dark, cured or grilled sausage such as a boerewors/blood-style or smoked sausage), piled on a white paper plate. Nothing else on this plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White paper plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side plate). Area = 3.14 x 10^2 = 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: One item, sliced sausage rounds (about 10-12 pieces, each roughly 3 cm across and 1-1.5 cm thick).

STEP 4 - Area: The sausage pieces cover roughly 45% of the plate, mostly piled in the centre. Food coverage ~45% of vessel (the pile is partly stacked, so the top-down footprint is a good approximation).

STEP 5 - Volume: Sausage footprint = 0.45 x 314 = 141 cm^2. Typical height of the pile (stacked rounds, around 2 cm) gives 141 x 2 = 282 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Sausage is dense meat, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 282 x 0.9 = 254 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sausage of this type is roughly 300 kcal per 100 g (fatty cured/cooked meat). 254 g x 3.0 = ~762 kcal.

Hmm, a cooked sausage this dense is usually closer to 250-300 kcal/100 g; I use 280 kcal/100 g: 254 x 2.8 = ~711 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 250 g of sliced sausage, roughly 700 kcal, is plausible for a fully plated portion of this size, though the visible amount may be somewhat less if the pile is shallower than assumed. I keep the estimate as is.

Estimated total: about 250 g, about 710 kcal.
